## 1. This week's analysis

```{r}
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("DESeq2")
```

```{r}
### 1. Load the counts

library(DESeq2)

counts_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RobertsLab/paper-tanner-crab/master/analyses/kallisto-0812/kallisto-0812.isoform.counts.matrix"
counts <- read.delim(counts_url, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

# kallisto gives estimated counts with decimals; DESeq2 needs whole numbers
counts <- round(counts)

dim(counts)   # 78,649 transcripts x 4 samples
head(counts)
```

```{r}
coldata <- data.frame(
  row.names   = colnames(counts),
  infection   = factor(c("uninfected", "infected", "uninfected", "infected")),
  temperature = factor(c("cold", "cold", "warm", "warm"))
)
coldata

# Stop here if the names don't line up
stopifnot(all(rownames(coldata) == colnames(counts)))
```

```{r}
### 3. Build the DESeq2 object

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts,
                              colData   = coldata,
                              design    = ~ infection)

# Levels are alphabetical by default, so "infected" would be the reference.
# Make "uninfected" the baseline so a positive log2FoldChange means higher in infected crabs.
dds$infection <- relevel(dds$infection, ref = "uninfected")

# Drop transcripts with almost no reads
dds <- dds[rowSums(counts(dds)) >= 10, ]
nrow(dds)
```

```{r}
### 4. Check sample structure before testing anything else
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = TRUE)
plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = c("infection", "temperature"))
```

```{r}
### 5. Test for differential expression

dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- results(dds, alpha = 0.05)

summary(res)
sum(res$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)   # number of significant transcripts
```

```{r}
### 6. Plot and save results

plotMA(res, ylim = c(-10, 10), main = "Infected vs uninfected")

res_df <- as.data.frame(res)
res_df$transcript_id <- rownames(res_df)
res_df <- res_df[order(res_df$padj), ]
head(res_df)

dir.create("output/week4", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(res_df, "output/week4/dge-results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

| Step                 | RNA-seq                                                                                                      | My project                                                                                                   |
|------------------|-----------------------|-------------------------------|
| Input                | RNA-seq FASTQ reads                                                                                          | 16S amplicon FASTQ reads                                                                                     |
| Analysis-ready table | Gene or transcript count table + sample metadata                                                             | ASV count table + sample metadata and taxonomy                                                               |
| Model/summary        | DESeq2 to identify differentially expressed genes or transcripts                                             | QIIME2 to summarize community composition, alpha diversity, and beta diversity                               |
| Interpretation       | Which genes or transcripts differ in expression between conditions, such as temperature or infection status? | How do bacterial communities differ between zoo-housed and wild polar bears, accounting for anatomical site? |

## 2. Reflection questions

1.  Why is sample metadata as important as the count matrix?

Without the metadata, we cannot make connections between the individual and the transcripts. For example, if we did not know an individual crab was infected or subject to different temperatures but it was expressing a specific gene, we wouldn't be able to connect that expression to their condition.

2.  What is the difference between statistical significance and biological importance in differential expression?

A statistically significant change is just based on a p value, often \< 0.05. However, the changes happening may be statistically significant but too small to have an impact in biological importance. One gene expression may be significant in analyses but have little to no impact on organism functioning.

3.  If your project is not RNA-seq, what is the equivalent of a count matrix and a results table in your workflow?

In my 16s metabarcoding project, the equivalent of the count matrix is probably the ASV table identifying unique sequences for each sample and then the assigned taxonomy which is essentially just telling us what ASVs were detected in each sample, the number of reads, and then what that can be assigned to taxonomically. A results table could either be the read count table with assigned taxonomy to each sample, or you could go deeper and identify alpha diversity values for each sample, taking the taxonomy data and exploring that further.
